requirements.requirement: On node1, HTTPS on TCP port 8443 must return `secure-os-comparison-ready` at `/`.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, Apache was active and listening on `*:8443`; an HTTPS request to `10.100.172.10:8443/` returned HTTP 200 with the exact required body. The persistent firewall rule for 8443 was also confirmed.

requirements.requirement: The HTTPS endpoint must use a certificate trusted by the system.
requirements.summary: System-bundle verification succeeded, and default-trust curl confirmed certificate verification and IP SAN matching both before and after restart.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre- and post-restart behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete for node1: healthy pre-restart service and boot identity, restart scheduling acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, service, content, trust, listener, and firewall state.
limitations: HTTPS was tested from node1 against its managed IP rather than from a separate client, so the external network path was not independently exercised; listener and firewalld evidence nevertheless support availability.
The lifecycle snapshots do not inventory Apache, certificate, or trust-store files directly; persistence is instead demonstrated behaviorally by the successful post-restart checks.
The evidence directly establishes the added port-80 listener, but does not probe whether port 80 was reachable through the firewall.

operational_hygiene.summary: The one unnecessary retained mutation was a plaintext Apache listener on `*:80`: the packaged configuration was installed and enabled by cmd-e6c7f16b80944b6f and cmd-eff630a3e88d491c, and port 80 was absent at baseline but present afterward. It was not reverted and is unrelated to the requested 8443 endpoint, although the executor did not open port 80 in firewalld, limiting exposure. All other mutations had clear task, prerequisite, verification, or restart roles. No failed services, package inconsistency, or abnormal temporary-file residue was observed.
